items.section: §8 Cardiovascular risk: lipids, apoB and Lp(a)
items.prompt: Antique anatomical steel-plate engraving in exactly the same style, ink colour and line technique as the reference images: fine parallel hatching and crosshatching, single muted sage-green ink on a pure white background, no colour fills, no gradients. Subject, two specimens side by side with clear white space between them, drawn like a classic anatomy-atlas plate: each is a short cut segment of a medium-sized artery shown in three-quarter perspective so the cut end faces the viewer and shows the wall in cross-section. On the left, a healthy artery with a thick, smooth, evenly layered muscular wall and a wide open round channel. On the right, the same artery with a crescent-shaped fatty plaque built up inside the wall on one side, a soft lumpy core beneath a thin smooth cap, bulging inward so the open channel is narrowed to about half its width and pushed off-centre. The channels are empty, no blood cells. Both specimens the same size and visual weight, floating on white. No text, no labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no numbers, no border, no signature.
items.alt: Engraving of two cut sections of an artery: on the left a healthy artery with a wide open channel; on the right a fatty plaque inside the wall narrowing the channel.
items.caption: How atherosclerosis develops: apoB-carrying particles lodge in the artery wall and build plaque over decades. Left, a healthy artery; right, plaque inside the wall narrowing the channel.

items.section: §3 Why bone and heart are part of the conversation
items.action: New plate after the 'Bone.' paragraph, before the bone-density chart
items.prompt: Antique anatomical steel-plate engraving in exactly the same style, ink colour and line technique as the reference images: fine parallel hatching and crosshatching, single muted sage-green ink on a pure white background, no colour fills, no gradients. Subject, two bone specimens side by side with clear white space between them, like a classic anatomy-atlas plate. On the left, a single human lumbar vertebra cut vertically down the middle, seen in three-quarter view, showing its dense smooth outer shell and the fine sponge-like lattice of trabecular bone filling the vertebral body. On the right, the upper end of a human thigh bone (the rounded femoral head, the neck and the greater trochanter) cut lengthwise, showing the thin outer cortex and the fine trabecular lattice inside the head and neck, the shaft fading out below. Both specimens the same visual weight, floating on white. No text, no labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no numbers, no border, no signature.
items.alt: Engraving of a lumbar vertebra and the top of a thigh bone, each cut open to show the sponge-like bone inside.
items.caption: The spine and the hip, where bone density is measured, cut open to show the lattice of bone inside.
